# Wiring and bring-up: PIR, arm button, LED, RTC battery

## Context
The PIR (HC-SR501), arm button, jumper wires and an XYGStudy RTC battery
have arrived. Nothing is wired yet. M3 used the mic and camera because the
PIR wasn't wired (M3-Status.md). The goal now is to wire the parts,
confirm each one works with the stock tools on the Pi, and then start the M4
code. That code is the button and LED in pird (Owen's area) and the arm
state machine in the hub (shared, DESIGN.md Section 4).

## As built (2026-11-13), all verified on the Pi
- PIR: brown VCC -> pin 2, orange GND -> pin 6, red OUT -> pin 11 (GPIO17).
  `gpiomon GPIO17`: rising on motion, falling a few s later, quiet when still.
- Button module (labels -, middle, S; middle pin unused): yellow S -> pin 13
  (GPIO27), blue - -> pin 14. `gpiomon --bias=pull-up GPIO27`: falling on
  press, rising on release (active low, as planned).
- RTC cell in J5 BAT. Cell type unknown (no label), so charging is left OFF.
  Power-cut test with no network: local time matched the phone after 3 min
  unplugged ("System clock synchronized: no", so the time came from the RTC).
  `hwclock` isn't installed; use `timedatectl`.
- No LED yet (GPIO22 / pin 15 kept free).

## Safety rules (every step)
- Shut down and unplug the Pi before connecting or moving any wire
  (`sudo poweroff`, then pull the USB-C).
- Never touch or unplug the CSI camera ribbon.
- The header's 5 V pins (2 and 4) must never touch a GPIO pin. A GPIO pin
  takes 3.3 V at most.

## Pin plan (Pi 5 40-pin header; pin 1 is the corner pin nearest the SD card)
| Part | Wire | Header pin | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| PIR HC-SR501 | VCC | pin 2 | 5 V |
| | GND | pin 6 | GND |
| | OUT | pin 11 | GPIO17 (pird's default `--line=17`) |
| Arm button | leg A | pin 13 | GPIO27 (internal pull-up, so a press reads low) |
| | leg B | pin 14 | GND |
| LED (later, not bought yet) | long leg (+) via 330 ohm resistor | pin 15 | GPIO22 (leave free) |
| | short leg (-) | pin 20 | GND |
| RTC battery | JST plug | J5 "BAT" connector on the board (next to USB-C) | n/a |

**No breadboard, so female-to-female jumper wires throughout.** The PIR's three
pins take the female ends directly. For the button, push one female end
onto each of two legs. With a 4-leg square tactile button, use two legs
that are **diagonally opposite**, because those are always on opposite
sides of the switch. If the jumper slips off the thin legs, bend the leg
slightly or crimp the connector gently with pliers. A button with
solder tabs or screw terminals needs the wires soldered or screwed on.
There's no LED for now. A plain LED plus a 220-330 ohm resistor costs
under $1 and can be added later on pins 15 and 20.

The PIR's output is 3.3 V, so it is safe on a GPIO pin even though the
sensor runs on 5 V. Set its time-delay knob fully anticlockwise (shortest)
and leave the sensitivity knob in the middle.

## RTC battery
1. Read the label on the cell. **ML**-xxxx means rechargeable. **CR**-xxxx
   means NOT rechargeable.
2. Only if it's ML: add `dtparam=rtc_bbat_vchg=3000000` to
   `/boot/firmware/config.txt` and reboot. Never enable charging on a CR cell.
3. Check that the clock survives a power cut: `sudo hwclock -r`, unplug for
   2 minutes with no network, boot, run `sudo hwclock -r` again, and confirm
   the time moved forward by about 2 minutes.

## Bring-up checks on the Pi (no project code involved)
- `gpioinfo` to find the header chip (gpiochip0 or gpiochip4) and see lines 17, 22, 27.
- PIR: `gpiomon -c gpiochip0 17` and wave a hand, after the PIR's 60 s warm-up.
- Button: `gpiomon -c gpiochip0 --bias=pull-up 27` and press it.
- LED (once you have one): `gpioset -c gpiochip0 22=1` lights it; Ctrl-C releases it.
- Then the real pipeline: `deploy/run-m3.sh` (PIR on) plus `build/pss events`
  shows a MOTION event. Paste the output: per CLAUDE.md, no hardware fixes
  get proposed without real evidence.

## Code (deferred: Bryan decides the pird/hub split when we get there)
- pird: request the button (27) and LED (22) lines along with the PIR. This
  is Owen's area, so he does it in his own session unless he explicitly
  hands it over.
- hub: the arm state machine DISARMED -> EXIT_DELAY (60 s, LED blinks) ->
  ARMED -> GRACE (30 s) from DESIGN.md Section 4 (shared). This needs its
  own plan and approval.
- Done = `make`, `make test`, `make asan` and `make netcheck` all pass.

Then the motion sensor test is complete. The sensor, the program, the hub, the camera and the storage all work together on real hardware.

**Next: the fusion code (camera only when motion and sound happen together).** Before I plan it, I need one decision from you. It's the question I mentioned earlier.

When someone comes in, the order is usually **door sound first** (the latch clicks), **then motion** as they walk into the sensor's view. With the 3-second window:

- **Sound then motion:** the moment motion happens, both are present, so the camera starts right away. No delay.
- **Motion then sound:** the camera has to wait until the sound arrives, up to 3 seconds late, and may miss the start.

My recommendation is to **start the camera only once both have happened**. It matches what you asked for exactly (motion alone or sound alone never turns the camera on), it matches your design document, and in the common case (door sound first) there's no delay at all.

The alternative is to start the camera on motion and delete the photos if no sound follows. That never misses the start, but the camera does switch on for motion alone.

Should I plan it the first way (camera only after both)? Reply in your own words. Then I'll read the hub code and write up the plan for you to approve before anything changes.
how would a door opening be delayed if you hear the sound but you also see the door open...?

You're right, and that's why the delay mostly doesn't happen. One detail, though: the motion sensor doesn't see the door. It detects **body heat moving**, and a door swinging isn't warm, so the door itself usually doesn't trigger it. It fires when the **person** steps into its view.

So a typical entry looks like this:
1. The handle or latch clicks: **sound**.
2. The door opens, and the person walks in: **motion**, a moment later.
3. At that moment both have happened, so the camera starts right away. **No delay.**

The delay only shows up in the reverse order: **motion first, sound later**. For example, someone already in the room walks past the sensor and then speaks or shuts a drawer. The system can't know yet whether a sound is coming, so it waits up to 3 seconds before deciding. That's not a door entry, so being a moment late there matters less.

So for door entries, "camera only when both happen" costs you basically nothing. That's why I recommend it. Should I go ahead and plan it that way?
how do you know it detects body heat moving???

It's in the sensor's name. **PIR** stands for **Passive InfraRed**, and that's how the HC-SR501 works:

- Everything warm gives off **infrared light**, which is invisible to our eyes. People give off a lot of it.
- Under the white dome sits a small sensor with **two halves** that measure infrared. The dome is a special lens that splits the room into zones.
- When something warm **moves** from one zone to the next, the two halves see different amounts of infrared for a moment, and the sensor fires. That's the **rising** you saw.
- "Passive" means it only receives. Unlike some sensors, it sends nothing out.

That's why it reacts to **heat that moves** and ignores both:
- **a warm thing that's still**, like you sitting perfectly still or a radiator, and
- **a cool thing that moves**, like a door or a curtain, *usually*.

Not perfectly, though. It can be fooled by anything that changes the heat pattern in its view: sunlight sweeping across a wall, a heater vent turning on, a pet. A door could set it off if it's a very different temperature from the room. Your design already plans to test this with the "fan-blown curtain" trials in DESIGN.md.

You can check it yourself: hold a book at arm's length so your hand and arm stay out of the sensor's view, wave the book in front of it, and watch `gpiomon GPIO17`. Then wave your bare hand. The hand should trigger it much more reliably.

Do you want to go ahead with "camera only when motion and sound happen together"?
yes we want to do camera only when motion and sound together
Got it. I'll read the code now to plan the change. Nothing gets changed until you approve the plan.

## 4. Analysis engine (`src/analysis`, all ours)

**Audio features (in `micd`).** 20 ms hops (882 samples) over a 1024-point Hann
window. Per frame: RMS, energy in 8 log-spaced bands (100 Hz – 8 kHz), and
spectral flux. FFT is a primitive (small library or our own radix-2).

**Background model.** Per band, an exponentially weighted mean and variance
(time constant ~60 s), updated only outside active events so a conversation
doesn't become "background". Frames are scored as per-band z-scores, so the
same device works next to a loud HVAC unit and in a silent room.

**Detectors.**
- *Impulse (latch/door):* spectral-flux z-score above `K_imp`, broadband, decay
  under 150 ms.
- *Voice:* z-score in the 300–3400 Hz bands above `K_voice` for ≥ 400 ms within
  2 s, with sub-200 Hz energy not dominant (rules out HVAC).
- *PIR:* HC-SR501 in **single-trigger mode** with the delay pot at minimum, so
  each detection is a pulse of a few seconds followed by a ~2.5 s low block
  time, even under continuous motion. A person moving around produces a train
  of pulses.

**Fusion state machine (in `hub`).**
```
IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (±T_co = 3 s around the edge; audio history checked)
MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed; durable at once)
MOTION_WINDOW --window expires, no audio--> MOTION_ONLY
IDLE --impulse/voice, no PIR within ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR pulse and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
```
Opening and closing use different conditions, so ten minutes of someone moving
around is one event, not forty.

**Arm state machine (in `hub`, button handled by `pird`).**
```
DISARMED --button--> EXIT_DELAY (60 s, LED blinks) --> ARMED (LED off)
ARMED --ENTRY confirmed--> GRACE (30 s) --button--> DISARMED, entry labelled `owner`
GRACE --30 s, no button--> ARMED, entry reported (routine / UNEXPECTED)
```
Events are only reported while ARMED. Macy can also use `pss arm` /
`pss disarm`. The LED stays dark while armed so the device doesn't draw
attention.

**Routine vs. unexpected (optional).** Housekeeping times are often unknown,
so the expected window is optional (`pss expect 10:00-14:00`). With no window,
every confirmed entry while armed is reported plainly; with one, entries
inside it are labelled `routine` and others `UNEXPECTED`. The device never
tries to identify who entered.

**Why a threshold cannot do this.** A loudness threshold fires on every
hallway door slam and misses a quiet entry in a noisy room; a PIR alone fires
on curtains moved by HVAC. The decision rests on the *timing* of two different
physical signals, scored against a background learned in *this* room, with
hysteresis on event boundaries. No single `if` reproduces that.

# Plan: camera only when motion AND sound coincide (fusion, M4)

## Context
Right now the hub fires the camera on motion alone or on sound alone. That
is the M3 stand-in in `src/hub/hub.c`: `open_event()` always calls
`trigger_burst()`. Bryan and Owen want photos only for a **confirmed
entry**, meaning a PIR rise and a sound onset within **T_co = 3 s** of each
other in either order. DESIGN.md Section 4 already says this ("the camera
only collects evidence for confirmed entries"; IDLE -> MOTION_WINDOW ->
ENTRY). Motion alone is logged as MOTION_ONLY and sound alone as
SOUND_ONLY, both **without photos**.

The audio signal stays the existing M3 sound onset in the hub. The impulse
and voice detectors are a separate M4 task and will plug into the same call
later.

## Design
The coincidence check works only on timestamps, so it doesn't matter which
message arrives first:
- Remember the time of the last PIR rise and the last sound onset (the
  sensors' own CLOCK_MONOTONIC `mono_ns`).
- On every rise, check for an onset within ±T_co. On every onset, check
  for a rise within ±T_co.
- If there's a match, the event becomes an ENTRY: make it durable with
  `store_event_open()` and fire the camera, once per event.
- Sound-then-motion (the usual door case) confirms the instant the person
  is seen. Motion-then-sound confirms when the sound arrives, at most 3 s
  later.
- An event already open as MOTION_ONLY or SOUND_ONLY is upgraded to ENTRY
  when a coincidence happens inside it. Closing is unchanged: 30 s with no
  activity, and never while a burst is pending.

## Changes
1. **New `src/analysis/fusion.h` / `fusion.c`** (Bryan's area). This is
   pure logic with no I/O, following the pattern of
   `src/capture/pir/pir_logic.c`.
   ```c
   struct fusion { int64_t t_co_ns, last_rise_ns, last_onset_ns; int have_rise, have_onset; };
   void fusion_init(struct fusion *f, int64_t t_co_ns);
   int  fusion_rise(struct fusion *f, int64_t ts_ns);   /* 1 = onset within ±T_co */
   int  fusion_onset(struct fusion *f, int64_t ts_ns);  /* 1 = rise within ±T_co */
   void fusion_forget(struct fusion *f, int pir, int mic); /* sensor disconnected */
   ```
2. **`src/hub/hub.c`** (shared):
   - `struct event` gets `uint32_t kind`, and `struct hub` gets
     `struct fusion fu` plus `int64_t t_co_ns`.
   - `open_event()` no longer calls `trigger_burst()`. It sets `kind` to
     MOTION_ONLY or SOUND_ONLY.
   - New `confirm_entry()`: sets `kind = PSS_EV_ENTRY`, writes the
     `store_event_open()` record (on a store failure it exits so recovery
     runs, the same as `close_event`), logs `event N: ENTRY confirmed
     (motion+sound dt=…ms)`, then calls `trigger_burst()`.
   - `on_pir_edge()` and `on_mic_frame()` call `fusion_rise()` and
     `fusion_onset()`, and call `confirm_entry()` on a match, opening the
     event first if none is open.
   - `close_event()` uses `ev->kind` for ENTRY. Otherwise it keeps the
     existing rule (`pir_edges > 0` gives MOTION_ONLY, else SOUND_ONLY),
     and its log line prints ENTRY.
   - `conn_drop()` for the PIR or mic calls `fusion_forget()`.
   - New option `--t-co-ms=3000`, added to `usage()` and the start log line.
3. **`Makefile`**: link `analysis/fusion` into the hub, and add the
   `test_fusion` binary to the test list.
4. **Tests.** The requirement changed, so the old expectations ("motion
   alone gives 3 photos") are now wrong. No coverage is removed: the camera
   checks move to an ENTRY test.
   - New `tests/test_fusion.c` (unit):
     - Rise then onset at +2.9 s matches; at +3.1 s it doesn't.
     - Onset then rise, in both directions.
     - Messages arriving out of order.
     - Exactly at T_co.
     - After `fusion_forget()`, no match.
   - `tests/test_e2e.c`:
     - `test_pir_to_storage`: PIR only gives MOTION_ONLY, 0 images, no
       clip directory and no NO_IMAGES flag. The boot count and event id
       checks stay.
     - `test_sound_to_storage`: fan noise still opens no event. The clap
       gives SOUND_ONLY with 0 images and no clip directory.
     - **New `test_entry_to_storage`**: the test acts as both pird and micd
       on two connections, with a short `--warmup-frames` and
       `--t-co-ms=500` to keep it fast. Four cases:
       (a) clap then PIR rise gives ENTRY, 3 images, and an EVENT_OPEN
       record on disk;
       (b) PIR rise then clap gives ENTRY;
       (c) rise and clap further apart than T_co give no ENTRY and no
       photos;
       (d) a second session with `FAKE_RPICAM_FAIL=1` gives ENTRY with
       NO_IMAGES. This is the camera-failure check moved over from
       `test_pir_to_storage`.
5. **`M3-Status.md` / DESIGN.md**: no change. DESIGN.md already describes
   this.

Not touched: pird, camd, micd (Owen's area), and the CLI. `pss events`
already prints ENTRY.

## Consequence to note
If the mic is unplugged or dead, no ENTRY can be confirmed, so **no photos
are taken at all** (events are still logged, flagged `audio-offline`).
That follows strictly from "both must happen". DESIGN.md's failure table
(micd crash gives DEGRADED events) doesn't say to fall back to motion-only
photos, so this plan doesn't either.

## Verification
- Lab machine: `make`, `make test`, `make asan`, `make memcheck` and
  `make netcheck` all pass. Show the output.
- On the Pi, run `deploy/run-m3.sh --mic --mic-device=plughw:CARD=Snowball`
  with the PIR wired, and wait past the PIR's 60 s and the mic's 5 s
  warm-ups:
  1. Wave only: `event N opened (PIR rise)`, no burst, and the event
     closes as MOTION_ONLY with images=0.
  2. Clap only, sensor covered: SOUND_ONLY with images=0.
  3. Clap, then wave within 3 s: `ENTRY confirmed`, burst, ENTRY with
     about 18 images.
  4. `build/pss events` shows all three.
- Commit (after green, and only if asked): "M4: camera fires only on
  confirmed ENTRY (PIR + sound within T_co)".

---
## Hardware as built (2026-11-13), all verified on the Pi
- PIR: brown VCC -> pin 2, orange GND -> pin 6, red OUT -> pin 11 (GPIO17).
- Button module: yellow S -> pin 13 (GPIO27), blue - -> pin 14; middle pin
  unused (Pi pull-up). Press = falling, release = rising.
- RTC cell in J5 BAT, type unknown, so charging is OFF. Kept time across a
  3 min power cut with no network (`timedatectl`; `hwclock` isn't installed).
- No LED yet (pin 15 / GPIO22 free).
- PIR through the real pipeline: event 4 MOTION_ONLY, 18 images, edge
  latency 20-33 us. The PIR re-fired every ~3 s while someone was in view,
  so the event only closed at Ctrl-C.

# Plan: camera only when motion AND sound coincide (fusion, M4)

## Context
Right now the hub fires the camera on motion alone or on sound alone. That
is the M3 stand-in in `src/hub/hub.c`: `open_event()` always calls
`trigger_burst()`. Bryan and Owen want photos only for a **confirmed
entry**, meaning a PIR rise and a sound onset within **T_co = 3 s** of each
other in either order. DESIGN.md Section 4 already says this ("the camera
only collects evidence for confirmed entries"; IDLE -> MOTION_WINDOW ->
ENTRY). Motion alone is logged as MOTION_ONLY and sound alone as
SOUND_ONLY, both **without photos**.

The audio signal stays the existing M3 sound onset in the hub. The impulse
and voice detectors are a separate M4 task and will plug into the same call
later.

## Design
The coincidence check works only on timestamps, so it doesn't matter which
message arrives first:
- Remember the time of the last PIR rise and the last sound onset (the
  sensors' own CLOCK_MONOTONIC `mono_ns`).
- On every rise, check for an onset within ±T_co. On every onset, check
  for a rise within ±T_co.
- If there's a match, the event becomes an ENTRY: make it durable with
  `store_event_open()` and fire the camera, once per event.
- Sound-then-motion (the usual door case) confirms the instant the person
  is seen. Motion-then-sound confirms when the sound arrives, at most 3 s
  later.
- An event already open as MOTION_ONLY or SOUND_ONLY is upgraded to ENTRY
  when a coincidence happens inside it. Closing is unchanged: 30 s with no
  activity, and never while a burst is pending.

## Changes
1. **New `src/analysis/fusion.h` / `fusion.c`** (Bryan's area). This is
   pure logic with no I/O, following the pattern of
   `src/capture/pir/pir_logic.c`.
   ```c
   struct fusion { int64_t t_co_ns, last_rise_ns, last_onset_ns; int have_rise, have_onset; };
   void fusion_init(struct fusion *f, int64_t t_co_ns);
   int  fusion_rise(struct fusion *f, int64_t ts_ns);   /* 1 = onset within ±T_co */
   int  fusion_onset(struct fusion *f, int64_t ts_ns);  /* 1 = rise within ±T_co */
   void fusion_forget(struct fusion *f, int pir, int mic); /* sensor disconnected */
   ```
2. **`src/hub/hub.c`** (shared):
   - `struct event` gets `uint32_t kind`, and `struct hub` gets
     `struct fusion fu` plus `int64_t t_co_ns`.
   - `open_event()` no longer calls `trigger_burst()`. It sets `kind` to
     MOTION_ONLY or SOUND_ONLY.
   - New `confirm_entry()`: sets `kind = PSS_EV_ENTRY`, writes the
     `store_event_open()` record (on a store failure it exits so recovery
     runs, the same as `close_event`), logs `event N: ENTRY confirmed
     (motion+sound dt=…ms)`, then calls `trigger_burst()`.
   - `on_pir_edge()` and `on_mic_frame()` call `fusion_rise()` and
     `fusion_onset()`, and call `confirm_entry()` on a match, opening the
     event first if none is open.
   - `close_event()` uses `ev->kind` for ENTRY. Otherwise it keeps the
     existing rule (`pir_edges > 0` gives MOTION_ONLY, else SOUND_ONLY),
     and its log line prints ENTRY.
   - `conn_drop()` for the PIR or mic calls `fusion_forget()`.
   - New option `--t-co-ms=3000`, added to `usage()` and the start log line.
3. **`Makefile`**: link `analysis/fusion` into the hub, and add the
   `test_fusion` binary to the test list.
4. **Tests.** The requirement changed, so the old expectations ("motion
   alone gives 3 photos") are now wrong. No coverage is removed: the camera
   checks move to an ENTRY test.
   - New `tests/test_fusion.c` (unit):
     - Rise then onset at +2.9 s matches; at +3.1 s it doesn't.
     - Onset then rise, in both directions.
     - Messages arriving out of order.
     - Exactly at T_co.
     - After `fusion_forget()`, no match.

       checks stay.
     - `test_sound_to_storage`: fan noise still opens no event. The clap
       gives SOUND_ONLY with 0 images and no clip directory.

       on two connections, with a short `--warmup-frames` and
       `--t-co-ms=500` to keep it fast. Four cases:

       record on disk;
       (b) PIR rise then clap gives ENTRY;

       photos;

5. **`M3-Status.md` / DESIGN.md**: no change. DESIGN.md already describes
   this.

already prints ENTRY.

# Wiring and bring-up: PIR, arm button, LED, RTC battery

## Context
The PIR (HC-SR501), arm button, jumper wires and an XYGStudy RTC battery
have arrived. Nothing is wired yet. M3 used the mic and camera because the
PIR wasn't wired (M3-Status.md). The goal now is to wire the parts,
confirm each one works with the stock tools on the Pi, and then start the M4
code. That code is the button and LED in pird (Owen's area) and the arm
state machine in the hub (shared, DESIGN.md Section 4).

## As built (2026-11-13), all verified on the Pi
- PIR: brown VCC -> pin 2, orange GND -> pin 6, red OUT -> pin 11 (GPIO17).
  `gpiomon GPIO17`: rising on motion, falling a few s later, quiet when still.
- Button module (labels -, middle, S; middle pin unused): yellow S -> pin 13
  (GPIO27), blue - -> pin 14. `gpiomon --bias=pull-up GPIO27`: falling on
  press, rising on release (active low, as planned).
- RTC cell in J5 BAT. Cell type unknown (no label), so charging is left OFF.
  Power-cut test with no network: local time matched the phone after 3 min
  unplugged ("System clock synchronized: no", so the time came from the RTC).
  `hwclock` isn't installed; use `timedatectl`.
- No LED yet (GPIO22 / pin 15 kept free).
- Real pipeline, PIR only (`deploy/run-m3.sh`, 16:17-16:20): pird warm-up
  over at T+60s; first rise -> `event 4 opened (PIR rise)` -> burst started
  3 ms later -> `burst 4 done: 18 frames` -> committed to clips/4.dir.
  The PIR kept re-firing (9 rises, pulses ~0.45 s, >= 2.5 s apart), so the
  event never got 30 s quiet; Ctrl-C closed it: `MOTION_ONLY dur=61.9s
  edges=9 images=18 audio-offline`, `hub: exit 0`. Edge latency 20-33 us
  (one 97 us during the burst).
- Seen in passing: rpicam-still prints a screenful of libcamera INFO per
  frame (camd, Owen's area); bursts still 18/20 frames (known).

## Safety rules (every step)
- Shut down and unplug the Pi before connecting or moving any wire
  (`sudo poweroff`, then pull the USB-C).
- Never touch or unplug the CSI camera ribbon.
- The header's 5 V pins (2 and 4) must never touch a GPIO pin. A GPIO pin
  takes 3.3 V at most.

## Pin plan (Pi 5 40-pin header; pin 1 is the corner pin nearest the SD card)
| Part | Wire | Header pin | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| PIR HC-SR501 | VCC | pin 2 | 5 V |
| | GND | pin 6 | GND |
| | OUT | pin 11 | GPIO17 (pird's default `--line=17`) |
| Arm button | leg A | pin 13 | GPIO27 (internal pull-up, so a press reads low) |
| | leg B | pin 14 | GND |
| LED (later, not bought yet) | long leg (+) via 330 ohm resistor | pin 15 | GPIO22 (leave free) |
| | short leg (-) | pin 20 | GND |
| RTC battery | JST plug | J5 "BAT" connector on the board (next to USB-C) | n/a |

**No breadboard, so female-to-female jumper wires throughout.** The PIR's three
pins take the female ends directly. For the button, push one female end
onto each of two legs. With a 4-leg square tactile button, use two legs
that are **diagonally opposite**, because those are always on opposite
sides of the switch. If the jumper slips off the thin legs, bend the leg
slightly or crimp the connector gently with pliers. A button with
solder tabs or screw terminals needs the wires soldered or screwed on.
There's no LED for now. A plain LED plus a 220-330 ohm resistor costs
under $1 and can be added later on pins 15 and 20.

The PIR's output is 3.3 V, so it is safe on a GPIO pin even though the
sensor runs on 5 V. Set its time-delay knob fully anticlockwise (shortest)
and leave the sensitivity knob in the middle.

## RTC battery
1. Read the label on the cell. **ML**-xxxx means rechargeable. **CR**-xxxx
   means NOT rechargeable.
2. Only if it's ML: add `dtparam=rtc_bbat_vchg=3000000` to
   `/boot/firmware/config.txt` and reboot. Never enable charging on a CR cell.
3. Check that the clock survives a power cut: `sudo hwclock -r`, unplug for
   2 minutes with no network, boot, run `sudo hwclock -r` again, and confirm
   the time moved forward by about 2 minutes.

## Bring-up checks on the Pi (no project code involved)
- `gpioinfo` to find the header chip (gpiochip0 or gpiochip4) and see lines 17, 22, 27.
- PIR: `gpiomon -c gpiochip0 17` and wave a hand, after the PIR's 60 s warm-up.
- Button: `gpiomon -c gpiochip0 --bias=pull-up 27` and press it.
- LED (once you have one): `gpioset -c gpiochip0 22=1` lights it; Ctrl-C releases it.
- Then the real pipeline: `deploy/run-m3.sh` (PIR on) plus `build/pss events`
  shows a MOTION event. Paste the output: per CLAUDE.md, no hardware fixes
  get proposed without real evidence.

## Code (deferred: Bryan decides the pird/hub split when we get there)
- pird: request the button (27) and LED (22) lines along with the PIR. This
  is Owen's area, so he does it in his own session unless he explicitly
  hands it over.
- hub: the arm state machine DISARMED -> EXIT_DELAY (60 s, LED blinks) ->
  ARMED -> GRACE (30 s) from DESIGN.md Section 4 (shared). This needs its
  own plan and approval.
- Done = `make`, `make test`, `make asan` and `make netcheck` all pass.

CC     ?= cc
BUILD  ?= build
SAN    ?=
CFLAGS  := -std=c17 -D_GNU_SOURCE -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wvla -O2 -g -Isrc -MMD -MP $(SAN)

HAVE_GPIOD := $(shell pkg-config --atleast-version=2.0 libgpiod 2>/dev/null && echo y)
HAVE_ALSA  := $(shell pkg-config --exists alsa 2>/dev/null && echo y)

COMMON := common/log common/time common/util common/ipc common/client
STORE  := store/crc32 store/dirlist store/evlog store/clip
obj = $(addprefix $(BUILD)/obj/,$(addsuffix .o,$(1)))

BINS := $(BUILD)/hub $(BUILD)/camd $(BUILD)/pss
ifeq ($(HAVE_GPIOD),y)
BINS += $(BUILD)/pird
endif
ifeq ($(HAVE_ALSA),y)
BINS += $(BUILD)/micd
endif

TESTS     := test_store test_ipc test_pir_logic test_features test_e2e
TEST_BINS := $(addprefix $(BUILD)/tests/,$(TESTS))
TEST_ENV  := PSS_BIN_DIR=$(abspath $(BUILD)) PSS_TEST_DIR=$(CURDIR)/tests

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck netcheck deploy clean

all: $(BINS)
ifneq ($(HAVE_GPIOD),y)
	@echo "note: libgpiod >= 2.0 not found; pird not built here (it builds on the Pi)"
endif
ifneq ($(HAVE_ALSA),y)
	@echo "note: ALSA not found; micd not built here"
endif

$(BUILD)/obj/%.o: src/%.c
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD)/obj/tests/%.o: tests/%.c
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD)/obj/capture/pir/pird.o: CFLAGS += $(shell pkg-config --cflags libgpiod 2>/dev/null)
$(BUILD)/obj/capture/mic/micd.o: CFLAGS += $(shell pkg-config --cflags alsa 2>/dev/null)

$(BUILD)/hub: $(call obj,hub/hub $(COMMON) $(STORE))
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@ -lm

$(BUILD)/camd: $(call obj,capture/cam/camd $(COMMON) store/dirlist store/clip)
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@

$(BUILD)/pss: $(call obj,cli/pss $(COMMON) $(STORE))
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@

3	 * $PSS_RUN_DIR/hub.sock, turns PIR edges into events, asks camd for an image
4	 * burst per event, and commits everything through the store (mechanism D).
5	 *
6	 * M3 scope: no fusion yet (needs collected data, M4). A PIR rise opens a
7	 * MOTION_ONLY event; a sound onset (below) with no PIR opens a SOUND_ONLY
8	 * event. Every successful burst is kept.
9	 *
10	 * M3 sound trigger (stand-in for DESIGN.md Section 4's detectors, M4): an
11	 * EWMA background model of spectral flux and log RMS, learned only while no
12	 * event is open. A frame is an onset when its flux z-score and its loudness
13	 * above the room background both pass thresholds, so steady noise (fans,
14	 * AC) never triggers: its flux stays near its own mean and its level is the
15	 * background. Thresholds are placeholders until tuned on Pi recordings.
16	 *
17	 * Exit codes: 0 on SIGTERM/SIGINT, 1 on error (including any store write
18	 * failure, so the supervisor restarts us and recovery runs), 2 on usage.
19	 */

HAVE_ALSA  := $(shell pkg-config --exists alsa 2>/dev/null && echo y)

STORE  := store/crc32 store/dirlist store/evlog store/clip
obj = $(addprefix $(BUILD)/obj/,$(addsuffix .o,$(1)))

ifeq ($(HAVE_GPIOD),y)
BINS += $(BUILD)/pird
endif
ifeq ($(HAVE_ALSA),y)
BINS += $(BUILD)/micd
endif

TESTS     := test_store test_ipc test_pir_logic test_features test_fusion test_e2e
TEST_BINS := $(addprefix $(BUILD)/tests/,$(TESTS))

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck netcheck deploy clean

all: $(BINS)
ifneq ($(HAVE_GPIOD),y)
	@echo "note: libgpiod >= 2.0 not found; pird not built here (it builds on the Pi)"
endif
ifneq ($(HAVE_ALSA),y)
	@echo "note: ALSA not found; micd not built here"
endif

$(BUILD)/obj/%.o: src/%.c
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD)/obj/tests/%.o: tests/%.c
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD)/obj/capture/pir/pird.o: CFLAGS += $(shell pkg-config --cflags libgpiod 2>/dev/null)
$(BUILD)/obj/capture/mic/micd.o: CFLAGS += $(shell pkg-config --cflags alsa 2>/dev/null)

$(BUILD)/hub: $(call obj,hub/hub $(COMMON) $(STORE))
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@ -lm

$(BUILD)/camd: $(call obj,capture/cam/camd $(COMMON) store/dirlist store/clip)
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@

$(BUILD)/pss: $(call obj,cli/pss $(COMMON) $(STORE))
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@

$(BUILD)/pird: $(call obj,capture/pir/pird capture/pir/pir_logic $(COMMON))
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@ $(shell pkg-config --libs libgpiod)

	@mkdir -p $(@D)

	@echo "== all tests passed ($(BUILD))"

# The lab machines' gcc lacks libasan; clang has a working runtime there.
ASAN_CC := $(shell command -v clang >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo clang || echo $(CC))
asan:

memcheck: $(TEST_BINS) $(BUILD)/hub $(BUILD)/camd
	@set -e; for t in $(TEST_BINS); do echo "== valgrind $$t"; \
		$(TEST_ENV) valgrind -q --error-exitcode=1 --leak-check=full \
		--errors-for-leak-kinds=definite,indirect $$t; done
	@echo "== memcheck clean"

	@if grep -rnE 'AF_INET|getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|curl|https?:' src/; then \
		echo "netcheck: FAIL (network API in src/)"; exit 1; fi
	@if grep -rnE '\bconnect\(' src/ | grep -v '^src/common/ipc.c:'; then \
		echo "netcheck: FAIL (connect() outside the AF_UNIX helper)"; exit 1; fi
	@echo "netcheck: OK (no network APIs in src/)"

deploy:

	rsync -a --delete --exclude .git --exclude build --exclude build-asan ./ $(PI):pss/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd pss && make'

clean:
	rm -rf build build-asan

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

content.text:
The fusion change is in and checked. The camera now fires only when motion and a sound happen within 3 seconds of each other. **Nothing is committed yet.**

**Checks:** `make`, `make test`, `make asan`, `make memcheck` and `make netcheck` all pass, output above. The one "burst failed" line is intended: it's the test where the camera is made to fail on purpose.

**What the new test showed, in order:**
- **Sound, then motion 0.1 s later:** `ENTRY confirmed (motion+sound, sound -0.1s from motion)`, 3 photos saved.
- **Motion, then sound 0.2 s later:** `ENTRY confirmed (… sound +0.2s from motion)`, 3 photos saved.
- **Motion and sound 1 s apart** (the test uses a 0.5 s window to run faster): `MOTION_ONLY … images=0`. No camera.
- **Camera broken:** the ENTRY is still saved, marked "no-images".

The motion-only and sound-only tests now expect **no** photos. That's the new rule, not a weakened test: the photo and camera-failure checks moved into the ENTRY test above.

**What changed:**
- [src/analysis/fusion.c](src/analysis/fusion.c) (new, your area): the 3-second matching rule.
- [src/hub/hub.c](src/hub/hub.c) (shared): events no longer fire the camera when they open. The camera fires once an event is confirmed as an ENTRY, and the ENTRY is saved to disk at that moment, so a power cut can't lose it. There's also a new `--t-co-ms` setting for the window (default 3000).
- [tests/test_fusion.c](tests/test_fusion.c) (new) and [tests/test_e2e.c](tests/test_e2e.c): the tests above.
- [Makefile](Makefile): builds and runs the new file and test.

**Still to do:**
- **Test on the Pi.** The Pi still runs the old code. Your Pi copy came over through `make deploy`, which needs the Pi's network address, so the new code has to be copied over the same way. Then we run the system with **both** the sensor and the mic: wave only (no photos), clap only (no photos), then clap and walk in (photos).
- **Commit.** Should I commit this as "M4: camera fires only on confirmed ENTRY (PIR + sound within T_co)"?
